navy:
Soviet Union / Russia (faction key `pact`) — SURFACE FLEET ONLY. 26 hulls with `layer:"sea"` carry `fac:"pact"`; six of those are the e20 hand-written roster in js/rules.js and twenty are generated per-era rows in js/eras.js. Submarines (pact_e50/e60/e80/e90/e00_sub, sub_p, ssbn_p, ssgn_p) are excluded — other workflows own them. Five nation-neutral `fac:"both"` sea hulls (lst, oiler, repair_sea, minesweeper, navminelayer) are fielded by pact but are shared across all eight factions; they are noted where relevant and flagged as cross-faction.

Everything below was resolved at runtime under JavaScriptCore over the concatenation `var window=this;` + util.js + config.js + facts.js + rules.js + eras.js + heavyair.js + generations.js, then read back out of UNITS/WEAPONS after generations.js had finished rewriting. Nothing here is read off a source line.

findings.whatTheGameHas: The weapon named "12 x P-700 Granit under the deck" (e90) and "P-700 Granit" (e00) resolves to warhead:"flak", proj:"missile", tgt {ground:0, air:1, sea:0, sub:0}. Measured under jsc, not read off a line. Kuznetsov's headline weapon can shoot down aircraft and cannot touch a ship — and it is the ONLY weapon either hull carries, so the Soviet/Russian carrier has no anti-surface capability of any kind in two eras.
findings.whatIsReal: P-700 Granit (SS-N-19 Shipwreck), in service 1983. Seven tonnes, Mach 2.5, 750 kg warhead, active radar seeker with salvo logic that lets one round climb and spot for the others. It exists for exactly one purpose: to kill an American carrier. Twelve are shipped in below-deck inclined tubes under Kuznetsov's flight deck, twenty in a Kirov, twenty-four in an Oscar II. It has no anti-air mode and no land-attack mode.
findings.fix: warhead "he", tgt {ground:0, air:0, sea:1, sub:0}; and append a real air-defence weapon, because Kuznetsov's actual SAM is 3K95 Kinzhal (SA-N-9), 192 rounds of 9M330 in 24 eight-cell revolvers — not Granit and not Shtil.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "14 x Ka-25 ASW helicopters", warhead:"flak", tgt {ground:0, air:1, sea:0, sub:0}. The ship's entire armament is an anti-submarine air group that cannot attack a submarine, and can only shoot at aeroplanes.
findings.whatIsReal: Moskva commissioned 1967, Leningrad 1969. Built around fourteen Ka-25PL Hormone-A for one job: hunting Polaris boats in the Eastern Mediterranean. The unit's own description in eras.js says so — "built to hunt Polaris submarines rather than project air power". Her air-defence weapon was a separate system, two twin B-187 launchers for M-11 Shtorm (SA-N-3), 48 rounds.
findings.fix: Make the air group tgt {ground:0, air:0, sea:0, sub:1} with warhead "he", and append an M-11 Shtorm entry for the air-defence job the mask had been doing under a false name.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Named "2 x RBU-6000" (e60) and "RBU-6000" (e90), both resolving to proj:"shell", speed 700, sfx "shot", tgt {ground:1, air:1, sea:1, sub:0}. The Grisha's rocket mortar can engage aircraft and cannot engage a submarine. The ship is the Soviet Navy's dedicated coastal ASW corvette and in the game it has no anti-submarine weapon at all.
findings.whatIsReal: RBU-6000 Smerch-2, 1961: a twelve-barrel 213 mm spigot mortar throwing RGB-60 depth bombs to about 5,800 m. It is an anti-submarine weapon and nothing else. The correct entry already exists in the repo — rules.js `asw_rbu`, name "RBU-6000 rocket mortar", tgt {ground:0, air:0, sea:0, sub:1} — roughly five thousand lines away, and the e20 destroyer_p and cruiser_p already carry it correctly.
findings.fix: The projectile block is a GUN (four-round bursts of shells at 700 m/s), so name it for the gun the hull actually mounts — twin 57 mm AK-725 on the Grisha III, 76 mm AK-176 on the Grisha V — and append the existing `asw_rbu` as the separate ASW weapon it is.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "2 x M-1 Volna SAM" with tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1, sub:0}. A surface-to-air missile that cannot engage aircraft, and can bombard the shore.
findings.whatIsReal: M-1 Volna (SA-N-1 Goa), the V-600 round on twin ZIF-101 launchers, entering service on the Kashin from 1962. It is the first Soviet naval area air-defence missile and it is the whole reason Project 61 exists as an escort — the eras.js description itself calls the Kashin "the first Soviet destroyer designed around missiles rather than guns" and notes "no meaningful anti-ship missile in the original fit". The gun battery was two twin 76 mm AK-726, a genuinely dual-purpose mount.
findings.fix: Rename the gun-shaped template entry to "2 x twin 76mm AK-726" with tgt {g1,a1,s1,u0} (the AK-726 really is dual-purpose), and append a real M-1 Volna entry with tgt {ground:0, air:1, sea:0, sub:0}.

findings.unit: every pact surface hull from e50 to e00 (20 rows)
findings.whatTheGameHas: Measured across all twenty generated pact sea rows: not one carries a weapon whose tgt mask is air-only. There is no fleet air-defence system on the Soviet side in any era before e20. The S-300F Fort does not exist in WEAPONS under any id, any name, in any file. The game therefore cannot distinguish a Slava or a Kirov — a multi-channel area air-defence cruiser — from a Nanuchka.
findings.whatIsReal: S-300F Fort (SA-N-6 Grumble), first to sea on Azov in 1977 and standard from Slava (1982) and Kirov (1980): eight below-deck revolver launchers, 64 rounds on a Slava and 96 on a Kirov, 5V55RM to about 75 km, and the 48N6 of Fort-M on Pyotr Velikiy to 150 km, directed by a Tomb Stone phased array. It is the one Soviet system in the Aegis conversation and it is the single most important thing about those two ships as warships. Below it sit M-1 Volna (1962), M-11 Shtorm (1967), M-22 Uragan (1980) and 3K95 Kinzhal (1991). The repo already half-knows: warship_specs.js gives pact_e80_cruiser vls:64 and pact_e90_cruiser vls:96, which are exactly those magazines.
findings.fix: Author the five-generation Soviet naval SAM ladder (Volna, Shtorm, Uragan, Fort, Kinzhal) and append each to the hulls that carried it. Deliberately give NOTHING to the Sverdlov, Kotlin, Riga, Osa and Molniya — they had no area air defence and that gap is the content.

findings.whatTheGameHas: FIXED_MAGAZINE is keyed on the BASE weapon id and entities.js:1428 reads it as `this.def.magazine[this.def.weapons[wi]]`. The DOMAIN pass in generations.js clones the weapon on every sea/sub unit whose navy is not scored at exactly 1.00, renaming it to `<base>__<unit>`. Measured at runtime: cruiser_p has magazine key `ssm_oniks` and weapons entry `ssm_oniks__cruiser_p` — no match. Ten of eleven entries are dead (cruiser_p, destroyer_p, corvette_p, missileboat_p, ssgn_p, missileboat_k, corvette_k, missileboat_r, corvette_r, missileboat_c). The single survivor is missileboat_n, because DOMAIN.nato.naval is exactly 1.00 and its clone is skipped.
findings.whatIsReal: The mechanic's own comment states the intent: "a fixed deck tube is not [reloaded below decks]: what is in the tubes when the ship sails is what she has... which is why a Slava's first salvo is terrifying and her second does not exist." A Slava's sixteen P-1000 in fixed inclined deck tubes genuinely cannot be reloaded at sea; nor can an Osa's four Termit, a Tarantul's four, or an Oscar's twenty-four Granit. That limitation is the defining tactical fact about the Soviet surface fleet and about every small missile combatant in the game.
findings.fix: Re-key each unit's magazine against its FINISHED weapons array, after the DOMAIN pass, matching `<base>__<unit>` back to `<base>`. One loop in generations.js. This is cross-faction: it restores the Korean, Taiwanese, Chinese and Oscar magazines at the same time.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Every Soviet anti-ship missile in the generated rosters resolves with ground:1 — P-35, P-15 Termit, P-120 Malakhit, P-500 Bazalt, P-700 Granit, P-1000 Vulkan. The whole Soviet surface fleet can strike a target ashore with its carrier-killers, in every era from 1962.
findings.whatIsReal: None of those rounds has a land-attack role in any variant. They are 500-750 kg-warhead anti-ship missiles with active radar seekers and no terrain reference, no mission planning and no GPS. The P-5 Pyatyorka was the land-attack sibling of the P-35 and it was a submarine weapon retired in the 1960s. The Soviet Navy's answer to a target ashore was naval gunfire — which is why the Sverdlov's twelve 152 mm and the AK-130's twin 130 mm genuinely are land attack and are already coded ground:1 correctly. After 1990 the answer was nothing at all until Kalibr.
findings.fix: Set tgt {ground:0, air:0, sea:1, sub:0} on all eight. Leave the gun entries alone — naval gunfire IS land attack and the game already has that right. Keep ground:1 on exactly one hull: the Buyan-M.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Grep of all 1,686 weapon entries: the string "Kalibr" appears once, inside the display name "8 x Kalibr or Oniks in VLS" on w_e00_pact_missileboat. There is no Kalibr weapon. In e20 the Russian fleet has no land-attack round of any kind — missileboat_p, corvette_p, destroyer_p and cruiser_p all carry `ssm_oniks`, and carrier_p carries no surface weapon at all. So the game gives the Soviet fleet land attack in exactly the places it never had it, and denies it in the one place it does.
findings.whatIsReal: 3M-14 Kalibr, in service from roughly 2012-2015: subsonic, terrain-following, 1,500 km-plus, fired from a UKSK cell that also holds the 3M-54 anti-ship member of the family. On 7 October 2015 four Project 21631 Buyan-M corvettes of the Caspian Flotilla fired 26 rounds into Syria — a deliberate demonstration that Russia could hold targets at risk from 950-tonne hulls in inland waters. The eras.js Buyan-M description already narrates this event correctly. Carriers: Buyan-M, Karakurt (22800), Admiral Gorshkov (22350), Admiral Grigorovich (11356R), Project 636.3 Kilo. NOT Slava, NOT Sovremenny, NOT Kuznetsov — none has a UKSK.
findings.fix: Author `lacm_kalibr_p` with tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1, sub:0}, profile "cruise", range just short of tlam_n's 19.0, and give it to the Buyan-M only. Russia's entire surface land-attack capability being one small boat is the correct and slightly embarrassing answer, not a gap to be padded.

findings.unit: pact carrier in e80 — unitFor("pact","carrier","e80") returns null
findings.whatTheGameHas: pact_e60_carrier (Moskva) is from:e60 to:e60 and pact_e90_carrier (Kuznetsov) is from:e90. Measured: the Soviet Union has no aviation ship of any kind in the 1980s. The decade with the most Soviet aviation ships is the one decade the game gives it none.
findings.whatIsReal: Project 1143 Kiev-class heavy aviation cruisers: Kiev 28 December 1975, Minsk 1978, Novorossiysk 1982, Baku (later Admiral Gorshkov) 1987 — four hulls, all in commission through the 1980s. Moskva and Leningrad served alongside them until 1996 and 1991. Kiev is 273 m, 45,000 t full load, a cruiser's bow with eight P-500 Bazalt launchers and an M-11 Shtorm battery forward of an angled flight deck aft carrying about a dozen Yak-38 Forger and sixteen helicopters. The Forger is the weak half and everyone knew it: vertical landing only, no radar, and in Indian Ocean heat it could barely lift fuel and a gun pod. The e60 Moskva description in the repo already forward-references "Project 1143 Kiev (1975) with Yak-38 Forger VTOL is the next step" — the roster simply never got the hull.
findings.fix: Add pact_e80_carrier as the Project 1143 Kiev, with its own weapon row and a warship_specs.js silhouette row, from:e80 to:e80 (Kiev and Minsk withdrawn 1993, Baku laid up 1995, so e90 correctly belongs to Kuznetsov).

findings.whatTheGameHas: from:e80 to:e80, so unitFor("pact","missileboat","e90") returns null. Russia has no missile boat in the 1990s. The same row's own description says "The game's `missileboat_p`, still in Russian service in the 2020s" — the prose and the service window contradict each other on one line.
findings.whatIsReal: Project 1241 Tarantul/Molniya: first hulls 1979-81, Project 12411 built in quantity into the early 1990s, Project 1241.8 Molniya with Kh-35 Uran commissioning from 1999. These boats were the backbone of Soviet and Russian light forces throughout the 1990s and a number are still in commission. There is no year since 1980 in which Russia had no missile craft.
findings.fix: Change to:"e80" to to:"e90" on that row. unitFor picks the newest available hull, so e00 and e20 still correctly resolve to the Buyan-M and to missileboat_p.

findings.unit: destroyer_p, cruiser_p, missileboat_p (e20, rules.js NAVY table)
findings.whatTheGameHas: All three carry `ssm_oniks`, "P-800 Oniks". Three separate contradictions with the file's own prose, all measured: (1) destroyer_p's description says "her Sunburn missiles are genuinely dangerous" — Sunburn is the NATO reporting name for the P-270 Moskit, not for Oniks; (2) FIXED_MAGAZINE at rules.js:3528 reads `cruiser_p: { ssm_oniks: 16 },   // sixteen P-1000 in deck tubes` — the comment names Vulkan and the key names Oniks, on the same line; (3) missileboat_p is a Project 1241 Molniya, which has never carried Oniks in any variant. This is exactly the defect found on the IFVs and on the American attack boats: one missile stamped across a roster regardless of hull.
findings.whatIsReal: Slava fires sixteen P-1000 Vulkan (or P-500 Bazalt on the earlier hulls) from fixed inclined deck tubes. Sovremenny fires eight P-270 Moskit from two quad mounts. Molniya fires P-15M Termit or, on the Project 1241.8 rebuild, four Kh-35 Uran. P-800 Oniks goes to sea on the Yasen (where the game's ssgn_p correctly keeps it), in the Bastion-P coastal battery, and on the modern small combatants.
findings.fix: Substitute per hull: cruiser_p -> a P-1000 Vulkan entry; destroyer_p -> a P-270 Moskit entry (which makes its own description true); missileboat_p -> a Kh-35 Uran entry. Leave ssgn_p on Oniks. corvette_p (Project 22160) can keep it — that ship sails with no anti-ship missile at all in its base fit and its description already says so.

findings.unit: cruiser_p and carrier_p (e20) both carry sam_shtil "9M317 Shtil-1"
findings.whatTheGameHas: Slava, Sovremenny and Kuznetsov are given the same air-defence missile, which flattens the one distinction that matters most among surface combatants after 1980. cruiser_p also carries vls:0 in the NAVY table while warship_specs.js gives the same ship vls:64 — the two tables disagree about whether Slava has a below-deck magazine.
findings.whatIsReal: Slava's system is S-300F Fort (SA-N-6), 64 rounds, and it is the reason she is a fleet air-defence cruiser rather than a large missile boat. Kuznetsov's is 3K95 Kinzhal (SA-N-9), 192 rounds of 9M330, plus eight Kashtan gun/missile mounts. Sovremenny's is M-22 Uragan (SA-N-7) with 9M38/9M38M1; the 9M317 Shtil-1 that `sam_shtil` names is a 2000s round, correct for an Admiral Gorshkov, a Talwar or the two Chinese Project 956EM hulls, and one generation early on a Soviet-built Sovremenny. The NAVY table's vls:0 is defensible about the anti-ship tubes and wrong about the SAM magazine; warship_specs.js's 64 and 96 are the better reading.
findings.fix: cruiser_p -> S-300F Fort; carrier_p -> 3K95 Kinzhal; destroyer_p -> M-22 Uragan. Keep sam_shtil in the table for the ships that genuinely carry 9M317.

findings.whatTheGameHas: No `service` field, no `from` field, so the ERA_TIMELESS loop at rules.js stamps from:"e50". A Project 21630 Buyan is buildable in a 1950 battle under its 2006 designation. This is the class of defect the brief warned about — a unit with no service field that the previous audit did not check.
findings.whatIsReal: Project 21630 Buyan, lead ship Astrakhan, commissioned 2006. The role's inclusion in ERA_TIMELESS is a deliberate and well-argued design decision — that comment even names the right 1950s article: "between a Project 183 and a Mk VI there is a diesel". The role is timeless; the designation is not.
findings.fix: Make the name generic and the full name span the line, e.g. name:"Coastal Gunboat", full:"Project 183 / Project 205P / Project 21630". A one-line change that keeps the mechanic and removes the date claim. The same applies to boat_n ("Mk VI Patrol Boat", 2015) — cross-faction.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "4 x 130mm SM-2-1 in twin mounts" with tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1, sub:0}. Identical mask to the Sverdlov's 152 mm main battery, because both come from the same per-era template.
findings.whatIsReal: The SM-2-1 was a stabilised dual-purpose twin mount with Yakor fire control and genuine anti-aircraft capability — it is one of the things that made Project 56 modern in 1955. The Sverdlov's B-38 152 mm was NOT anti-aircraft, which is precisely why the Sverdlovs also carried twelve 100 mm SM-5 in separate AA mounts. So air:0 is correct for the cruiser and wrong for the destroyer, and the template gave them the same answer.
findings.fix: tgt {ground:1, air:1, sea:1, sub:0} on the Kotlin only. Leave the Sverdlov at air:0 — that one is right.

findings.whatTheGameHas: A live entry in WEAPONS with name "n/a", dmg 143, range 10.1. Its unit pact_e00_destroyer is deleted at load time by purgePhantomUnits(), so nothing references the weapon; measured, no dangling reference results. It is dead data with a placeholder name that could surface in a debug listing.
findings.whatIsReal: Nothing — the row exists only to satisfy the generator's per-era shape. The unit it belonged to correctly records that Russia laid down no new destroyer class after 1994.
findings.fix: Harmless. Delete it if the weapon table is ever swept, or leave it; it costs nothing but a confusing name.

findings.whatTheGameHas: The same ship appears three times with three different hulls: pact_e90_carrier len:305 beam:35.4; pact_e00_carrier len:270 beam:72; carrier_p len:270 beam:35.4. The e00 row mixes a waterline length with a flight-deck beam, which gives the silhouette builder a hull 270 m long and 72 m wide.
findings.whatIsReal: Admiral Kuznetsov: 305 m overall, 270 m waterline; 72 m maximum beam at the flight deck, 35.4 m at the waterline. The neighbouring rows use waterline beam (Slava 20.8, Sovremenny 17.3), so 35.4 is the figure that belongs in that column.
findings.fix: pact_e00_carrier beam:72 -> beam:35.4, and pick one length convention across all three rows (305 overall, or 270 waterline).

findings.unit: lst (fac:"both") — fielded by pact from e50
findings.whatTheGameHas: The Soviet and Russian landing craft in every era from 1950 is named "LCAC Air-Cushion Landing Craft". Cross-faction: the same row serves all eight navies.
findings.whatIsReal: The LCAC is an American air-cushion craft that entered service in 1986. The Soviet equivalents are the Project 770 Polnocny LCT (1967) and the Project 1232.2 Zubr air-cushion ship (1988); before either, the Project 450 and MP-series landing ships. Nothing resembling an LCAC existed anywhere in 1950.
findings.fix: Make the `full` generic — e.g. "Landing craft, mechanised / air-cushion" — rather than naming one nation's 1986 type. Flagged rather than edited: it is a fac:"both" row and a rename touches every navy, so it belongs to a cross-faction pass.

findings.unit: all twenty generated pact sea rows, e50-e00
findings.whatTheGameHas: Riga 1954, Kotlin 1955, Sverdlov 1952, Grisha 1970, Kashin 1962, Kynda/Grozny 1962, Osa 1961, Moskva 1967, Nanuchka 1970, Tarantul/Molniya 1979, Sovremenny 1980, Slava 1982, Pyotr Velikiy 1998, Steregushchiy 2008, Buyan-M 2014.
findings.whatIsReal: Every one of those matches the real first-of-class commissioning date, and every from:/to: window puts the hull in the right decade. Checked individually. The descriptive prose is also accurate and often sharp: the Kynda's lack of at-sea reload, the Slava's fixed deck tubes and topside radar clutter, Kuznetsov's ski-jump and Montreux-driven 'aviation cruiser' designation, the Sovremenny boiler failures, the Osa's ancestor sinking Eilat in October 1967.
findings.fix: None. This half of the roster was done carefully and is sound — the defects are all in the ARMAMENT table, not the hull table.

findings.whatTheGameHas: pact_e00_destroyer is authored with name "none new" and full "No new Russian destroyer class since 1994", and purgePhantomUnits() deletes it at load so it cannot be bought, then extends pact_e90_destroyer's `to` to e00 so the Sovremenny stays in service. Verified at runtime: the unit is gone and pact_e90_destroyer.to === "e00".
findings.whatIsReal: Russia has commissioned no new destroyer-sized surface combatant since 1994. The Lider programme was never funded; the real modern surface combatants are the Project 11356R and 22350 frigates. This is exactly the realism-over-symmetry outcome the owner asked for, implemented correctly, with the distinction between 'no new destroyers' and 'no destroyers' handled properly.
findings.fix: None. This is the model for how the rest of the audit's gaps should be recorded.

findings.unit: corvette_p and every pact sea hull carrying navgun_76
findings.whatTheGameHas: The NAVGUN loop in generations.js substitutes a per-faction gun into any sea/sub weapon whose name matches /OTO 76mm/. corvette_p resolves to "AK-176 76mm", dmg 50, acc 0.80 — measured, not assumed.
findings.whatIsReal: Project 22160 mounts the AK-176MA, not the Italian OTO Melara Super Rapid. The loop's own comment states the problem and the fix, and gives Britain the 4.5in Mk 8 and deliberately no entry for France or Germany because both really do buy the Italian gun. The foreign-weapon defect class was already found and correctly handled for naval guns.
findings.fix: None.

findings.whatTheGameHas: pact_e80_cruiser (Slava) vls:64, launchers:"box"; pact_e90_cruiser (Pyotr Velikiy) vls:96, launchers:"vls"; pact_e90_carrier (Kuznetsov) vls:12; Sverdlov guns:4 gunCal:152; Kotlin 2 x 130; Osa len 38.6 beam 7.6; Sovremenny 156.4 x 17.3.
findings.whatIsReal: Slava has 64 S-300F rounds in eight below-deck revolvers and her anti-ship rounds in fixed deck boxes — exactly vls:64 plus launchers:"box". Pyotr Velikiy has 96 Fort/Fort-M cells. Kuznetsov has 12 Granit tubes under the deck. Every dimension checked matches. This file is the most accurate naval table in the repo and it already encodes the S-300F magazine the armament table is missing.
findings.fix: None — and it should be treated as the reference when the SAM ladder is added, because it already knows the answer.

findings.unit: e20 NAVY table: pact vls:0 on every hull; no pact missileboat in e50; no pact carrier in e50
findings.whatTheGameHas: corvette_p, destroyer_p, cruiser_p and carrier_p all carry vls:0 while destroyer_n has 96 and cruiser_n 122, destroyer_c 64 and cruiser_c 112. unitFor returns null for a pact missileboat in e50 and a pact carrier in e50.
findings.whatIsReal: No Russian Navy surface combatant in service has a Mk 41-equivalent universal VLS farm of that depth; the UKSK cells on Gorshkov and Buyan-M are 16 and 8. The shape — NATO and the PLA deep, Russia shallow — is right. Project 183R Komar entered service in 1960 and Moskva in 1967, so neither a Soviet missile boat nor a Soviet aviation ship belongs in the 1950s. These are content, not defects.
findings.fix: None.

edits.why: FATAL + MAJOR, one block. Fixes the six inverted target masks (Granit firing at aircraft on Kuznetsov, the Moskva air group unable to attack submarines, the Grisha's RBU-6000 unable to attack submarines, the Kashin's Volna unable to engage aircraft), strips the land attack the Soviet anti-ship missiles never had, authors the missing Soviet naval SAM ladder including the S-300F Fort, authors Kalibr, and corrects the e20 Slava/Sovremenny/Molniya/Kuznetsov identities. Placed in generations.js because that is the file the codebase already uses for corrections of this shape (the NAVGUN loop, IFV_ATGM, setW), and placed BEFORE the DOMAIN pass so the naval quality multiplier and privateWeapon() see the corrected fleet. FATAL, independent of the block above and applicable on its own. Re-keys every unit's fixed deck magazine against the finished weapons array. Must sit AFTER the DOMAIN pass, which is why it anchors here. Cross-faction: restores the Soviet, Korean, Taiwanese and Chinese magazines and the Oscar's at the same time. Measured before the fix: unitFor("pact","carrier","e80") returned null, so the Soviet Union had no aviation ship in the one decade it had the most of them — four Kiev hulls (1975, 1978, 1982, 1987) with Moskva and Leningrad still in commission. proof:
HOW EACH CLAIM WAS ESTABLISHED — measured versus inferred, kept separate.

MEASURED (resolved at runtime under JavaScriptCore over `var window=this;` + util.js + config.js + facts.js + rules.js + eras.js + heavyair.js + generations.js, then read out of UNITS/WEAPONS):

1. THE TEMPLATE. Dumped every `w_<era>_<fac>_<role>` naval weapon for all five generated eras and all eight factions and printed proj / speed / warhead / sfx / burst / aoe / tgt beside the name. Result: inside a role, every one of those fields is constant across every faction and every era, varying only by a small per-faction constant (pact destroyers all burst 4 / aoe 1 / speed 700 / sfx cannon; NATO destroyers all burst 2 / aoe 0.9 / speed 720). The `name` string is the only field that tracks the weapon. That is the proof that the six inverted masks are one defect, not six, and it is the same defect as the IFVs and the American attack boats. Sample lines: `w_e60_pact_destroyer proj=shell spd=700 wh=he sfx=cannon burst=4 aoe=1 tgt{1,0,1,0} "2 x M-1 Volna SAM"` and `w_e90_pact_carrier proj=missile spd=520 wh=flak sfx=missile burst=1 tgt{0,1,0,0} "12 x P-700 Granit under the deck"`.

2. THE ERA GAPS. Built an 8-faction x 5-role x 6-era matrix by calling the game's own `unitFor(fac, role, era)`. pact carrier reads Y at e60, blank at e80, Y at e90/e00/e20. pact missileboat reads Y at e60/e80, blank at e90, Y at e00/e20. Both confirmed by direct null returns. The same matrix shows that gaps elsewhere are honest (GBR has no cruiser after e60, DEU has no carrier ever, KPA has no destroyer ever), which is what distinguishes these two from design.

3. THE DEAD MAGAZINE. Printed each FIXED_MAGAZINE unit's `magazine` keys beside its resolved `weapons` array. cruiser_p: `mag[ssm_oniks]` against `weapons: navgun_ak130__cruiser_p, sam_shtil__cruiser_p, ssm_oniks__cruiser_p, ...` — no match. Ten of eleven read `** NONE MATCH **`; only missileboat_n matched, and DOMAIN.nato.naval === 1.00 is the reason (the DOMAIN pass does `if (acc === 1 && rng === 1) continue;` before cloning).

4. THE PHANTOM PURGE. `UNITS["pact_e00_destroyer"]` is false at runtime and `UNITS["pact_e90_destroyer"].to === "e00"`, confirming purgePhantomUnits() deleted the "none new" placeholder and extended the previous generation. `WEAPONS["w_e00_pact_destroyer"].name === "n/a"` confirms the orphan weapon survives.

5. THE NAVGUN LOOP. corvette_p's first weapon resolves to id `navgun_76__corvette_p__corvette_p` with name "AK-176 76mm" — the OTO Melara has already been replaced on pact hulls.

6. ABSENCE OF AREA AIR DEFENCE AND OF KALIBR. Walked all twenty generated pact sea rows: no weapon with an air-only tgt mask. Walked all 1,686 WEAPONS entries: no id or name containing "S-300F", "Fort", "SA-N-6", "Volna", "Shtorm", "Uragan" or "Kinzhal"; "Kalibr" occurs once, inside the display string "8 x Kalibr or Oniks in VLS".

7. THE PROPOSED EDITS WERE APPLIED AND RUN. The repo was copied to a scratch directory (no file in /Users/hjiang/Desktop/redalert was written or edited) and every edit above was applied there. Under jsc: no exception, 0 dangling weapon references across 1,133 units and 1,717 weapons (baseline 1,132 / 1,686; the +1 unit is the Kiev and the +31 weapons are 11 new entries and 20 per-unit clones), and the same 21 pre-existing all-zero-tgt entries as the baseline, all of them mine-scattering cargo rounds. The post-fix per-era resolution reads correctly in all six eras — e.g. e80 cruiser now "16 x P-500 Bazalt in fixed deck tubes {0010} | S-300F Fort (SA-N-6) {0100}", e60 carrier "14 x Ka-25PL Hormone-A {0001} | M-11 Shtorm (SA-N-3) {0100}", e20 missileboat "Kh-35 Uran {0010} | 3M-14 Kalibr {1010}". All eleven FIXED_MAGAZINE entries resolve after the re-key.

8. BROWSER CHECKS. With the first and largest generations.js block applied to the scratch copy, the behaviour suite reported "==== 52 passed, 0 failed ====" and "runtime errors: NONE", and index.html's `errbox` came back empty.

9. ANCHOR UNIQUENESS. Every anchor in the edits above was counted with python3 `str.count` against the real repo file, not grep. All seven return exactly 1. One anchor had to be lengthened: `"from":"e80","to":"e80","service":"1979","confidence":"medium"` returns 2 (the other hit is w_e80_nato_spg), so the Molniya anchor was extended to include the weapons and prereq fields, which returns 1.

INFERRED, not measured — the historical half. Every commissioning date, magazine depth, missile range and system fitting cited above (Kiev 28 December 1975; Slava's 64 S-300F rounds and Pyotr Velikiy's 96; Kuznetsov's 192 rounds of 9M330 in 24 revolvers and twelve Granit tubes; Moskva's fourteen Ka-25PL; the Kashin's twin ZIF-101 and AK-726 mounts; the 7 October 2015 Caspian strike) comes from my own knowledge of these ships, not from anything in the repo. It is the part a reviewer should check. What the repo can confirm on its own is narrower but useful: warship_specs.js independently records vls:64 for the Slava, vls:96 for Pyotr Velikiy and vls:12 for Kuznetsov, which corroborates the S-300F and Granit magazines from a second table written by a different pass; and the eras.js descriptions independently name the Kiev and the Yak-38 as the Moskva's successor, name Sunburn on the Sovremenny, and call the Buyan-M's Caspian strike out by date.

The game-balance figures I authored — damage, range in tiles, reload, accuracy, intercept — are judgements placed on the existing naval scale, not facts. They were anchored to the entries already in rules.js (SM-2 at 150 km is 14.5 tiles, Shtil at 50 km is 11.0, Tomahawk at 1,600 km is 19.0) and authored at NATO-equivalent quality deliberately, because DOMAIN.pact.naval = 0.72 is the mechanism that is supposed to express Russian naval inferiority and doing it twice would double-count it.
risks: The behaviour suite was verified green (52 passed, 0 failed, runtime errors NONE) and index.html's errbox verified empty with the FIRST generations.js block applied. The later additions — the e20 identity swaps, the Kalibr, the magazine re-key, and the Kiev hull with its warship_specs row — could NOT be re-checked in Chrome: the machine accumulated roughly fifty orphaned headless Chrome processes that the sandbox will not let me kill, and after that point every run exceeded the tool's 120-second ceiling, including a control run of the UNPATCHED repo, which is how I know the slowdown is the machine and not the edits. Those later pieces are verified under jsc only: no exception, no dangling weapon reference, correct per-era resolution. Re-run the suite and the load check before committing, and kill the stray Chrome processes first.

The Kiev's warship_specs.js row uses bow:"raised" with super:"island", a combination no existing row uses (Moskva is raised+boxy, Kuznetsov is carrier+island). warship3d.js builds a silhouette by switching on those enums, so this pairing has never been exercised. It did not throw under jsc, but jsc never runs the 3D builder. If the Kiev renders wrong, bow:"carrier" is the safe fallback — at the cost of losing the thing that makes a Kiev a Kiev, which is a cruiser's bow in front of a flight deck.

The `ground:1` convention on anti-ship missiles is NOT confined to the Soviet roster. ssm_harpoon, ssm_nsm, ssm_yj18, ssm_hf3 and ssm_kn01 all carry it too, and so do the generated NATO, PLA, ROC and KPA naval weapons. I have only stripped it from the pact rounds, because pact is my remit. If the convention is deliberate — a ship shooting at a coastal target — then my edit makes the Soviet fleet the only one that cannot, which is a real asymmetry the owner should decide on rather than inherit from me. My reading is that it is the template leaking, not a convention, but that call belongs to whoever owns the other seven navies.

The same per-role template defect is visible on every other faction and I have not touched it. The clearest case: w_e90_nato_destroyer is named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk" and resolves to tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1, sub:0} — an Aegis destroyer that cannot engage aircraft, with the same shape of error as the Kashin. The whole generated naval armament table probably needs the pass I have just done for pact, done seven more times.

The magazine re-key is cross-faction by construction: it restores the fixed deck magazines for the KPA, Taiwanese, Chinese and Oscar hulls as well as the Soviet ones. That is the correct fix, but it changes those factions' behaviour in a way their owners have not reviewed — the affected craft go from an unlimited deck magazine to four or eight rounds. Worth flagging to whoever owns them before it lands.

I have given the e20 Kuznetsov (carrier_p) no anti-ship weapon, matching what the roster already had. The twelve Granit tubes were reportedly removed or plated over during the refit begun in 2017, so leaving her without them is defensible, but the sourcing on that is thin and contested. If the owner wants them back, ssm_granit_p now exists and one addNaval call adds it.

sam_fort_p's range of 12.6 tiles sits between the game's Shtil (11.0) and SM-2 (14.5). That is a judgement about how much of the Aegis advantage is the missile and how much is the sensor and the datalink, not a measured figure, and it is the single number in this package most likely to need tuning after play. Note also that DOMAIN.pact.naval = 0.72 then trims it to 12.1 at e20 — the multiplier is applied on top, not instead.

The `lst` landing craft is named "LCAC Air-Cushion Landing Craft" — an American 1986 hovercraft serving as the Soviet landing craft from 1950 — and I have deliberately NOT edited it, because it is a fac:"both" row shared by all eight navies and a rename touches every one of them. It needs a cross-faction owner. The same is true of the generic `minesweeper` and `navminelayer`: mine warfare is in my brief, and the honest finding is that the game models it nation-neutrally, so there is no Soviet-versus-NATO distinction to audit.
